title: Effect (L2 record)
description: A first-class scientific phenomenon between an L1 mechanism and its L3 realizations. This is not a measured product outcome; implementations[].observed_effects remains reserved for telemetry.

grade_basis.description: What corpus evidence the grade rests on, in the owner's words. A letter with no stated basis is an assertion; the reader of the record must be able to see whether it came from one secondary source or from replicated primary work. Optional while grades are still owner-corrected by hand; required once the computed rubric lands.

spanRole.description: What the quoted span is DOING in the source it was cut from (D-129). A verbatim quote can still misrepresent a paper: a sentence stating what a theory PREDICTS is background even when the same paper later confirms it, and some papers report the opposite of the prediction they open with. Only span_role=finding reports what the cited source itself observed, and only a finding can ground a fact. Optional so items written before D-129 stay valid — absent means the item predates the decision, which is a different fact from a role nobody could determine — but REQUIRED in code of anything the extraction pipeline produces, enforced in lib/span-role.ts and tools/validate.ts exactly as source_span is under D-110.

provenanceSourceSpan.description: Where the quote sits in its source record, and which version of that record the offsets were resolved against (D-110). Approval copies provenance verbatim out of the proposal, so the authoritative effect record stays independently verifiable: re-slicing lib/proposal-quality evidenceSourceText(record) at start/end must reproduce quote_or_locus byte for byte, and source_text_sha256 must still match that text. A hash mismatch marks the span STALE rather than letting the offsets quote different words.
